items.item: The unsafe function's own one real unsafe operation (`self.data.get_unchecked(index)`) is wrapped in its own explicit `unsafe { }` block with its own `// SAFETY:` comment, even though the whole function is already marked unsafe, which is exactly what Rust 2024's own `unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn` default warning requires.

The six real properties unsafe code must prove (validity, aliasing, initialization, lifetime, alignment, thread-safety) are named and briefly explained in post-notes rather than all individually measured here, since this topic's own guard directly demonstrates only the initialization/bounds property; the other five get their own full, direct treatment in topic 78.

'This is faster' being insufficient as a safety argument is explained in post-notes by contrasting it directly with Chapter 29's own performance-measurement topics, since speed and soundness are two genuinely separate claims a single function can satisfy independently of each other.

All of this topic's own measured claims run entirely on plain in-memory Rust values, a plain fixed-size array, and a plain `Cell<u64>` counter, with no file, network, root access, or actual undefined behavior executed; 'the contract', 'the guard', and 'the call counter' are all real, deterministic Rust values, continuing this domain's own established pattern.
